::: {.hero}
# Direct, don't type.

::: {.lead}
The future of research programming is shifting from writing every line to **directing, reviewing, and iterating with intelligent agents.**
:::

This three-hour, hands-on SMDM short course teaches you to work with AI agents like **Claude Code** and **OpenAI's Codex** — with **git & GitHub** as your safety layer — and ends with you building a custom workflow for your own research.

[Start the pre-work →](setup.qmd){.btn-course} [Join the Slack community](https://join.slack.com/t/agenticaiworkinggroup/shared_invite/zt-45afgdq1j-R8PNZz3SqUZuzgamkYDttQ){.btn-course .ghost}
:::

## Get ready: three pieces of pre-work

The course is hands-on from the first hour, so arriving set up is everything. Work through these three steps in order — budget about an hour total. When you finish each one, post in the [course Slack channel](https://join.slack.com/t/agenticaiworkinggroup/shared_invite/zt-45afgdq1j-R8PNZz3SqUZuzgamkYDttQ).

*First, though:* take the **[2-minute baseline survey](survey.qmd)** — it shapes how I pitch the course.

::: {.grid}
::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-4}
::: {.path-card}
**① Set up your machine**

~30 min, done once. Install git, create a GitHub account, connect them with SSH keys, and install the `gh` CLI plus an AI agent — **Claude Code or Codex, your choice**. Ends with a verification checklist.

[Setup guide →](setup.qmd)
:::
:::
::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-4}
::: {.path-card}
**② Play the Terminal Trainer** 🎮

~20 min, in your browser, nothing to install. Nine missions that teach every terminal and git command we'll use — through your first pull request. Win the 🏆.

[Play now →](game.qmd)
:::
:::
::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-4}
::: {.path-card}
**③ Git & GitHub Basics**

~20 min read + 15 min practice. What version control actually is, the mental model of a repository, and the branch → pull request → merge workflow the whole course runs on.

[Read it →](git-basics.qmd)
:::
:::
:::

## Who this is for

Researchers and academics who want to work faster and more reproducibly with AI agents — whether that's building simulation models, cleaning data, producing figures and tables, managing analysis pipelines, or drafting and revising manuscripts. **No programming experience required.** Agents meet you where you are: if you can describe what you want, you can direct one. The pre-work below covers every technical skill the course assumes.

## What to expect on course day

Details will unlock here on course day — but the shape is: short lectures, live demonstrations, and hands-on exercises, ending with a build session where you prototype an agentic workflow around **your own research task**. You'll leave with working skills and a real prototype.

::: {.callout-important}
## Two things to bring
1. **A set-up laptop** — all three pre-work steps done, verification checklist passing.
2. **A research task in mind** — a simulation model, a data-cleaning pipeline, a figure you keep remaking, a reviewer response. The last part of the course is yours to build on it.
:::
